panels.title: Public API
panels.description: Blackbox probe of /healthz every 2m -- the liveness signal.

panels.title: Data volume
panels.description: From helpers/volume_guard.sh via the node-exporter textfile collector. 0 means Postgres may be on an empty root-disk cluster while /healthz still returns ok.

panels.title: Scrape targets up
panels.description: blackbox-stats is EXCLUDED: it scrapes every 20m, so its series is stale for most of that window and would make this flap between 5 and 6. Its health is covered by its own alert.

panels.title: Cert expires in
panels.description: tls internal issues 12-HOUR certs, so ~9-12h here is NORMAL. Alert threshold is deliberately 1h.

panels.title: OOM kills (1h)
panels.description: Host has ZERO swap - OOM kills are abrupt.

panels.title: Cache entries
panels.description: Baseline 2026-08-22: 465,433. A collapse here is the data-side signature of the volume boot race.

panels.title: A3M total
panels.description: Sum of a3m_size_bytes over status='active' entries -- the rows that have live objects on OSDF.

panels.title: Capacity used
panels.description: Against 50 TB (decimal). If the quota is actually TiB, this reads ~10% high.

panels.title: Projected time to full
panels.description: Linear extrapolation of the last 7 days of growth. Needs about a week of history to mean anything; negative or absent means storage is flat or shrinking.

panels.title: Growth / day
panels.description: Bytes added per day, from the same 7d linear fit.

panels.title: A3M bytes by source
panels.description: Stacked, so the top of the stack is total consumption.

panels.title: Capacity used (%)
panels.description: Watch the slope, not the value -- at 5.9% the slope is what tells you when to ask for more quota.

panels.title: Cache hit ratio (all time)
panels.description: The headline number. hits/sequences, both counted per SEQUENCE. Note the query_metrics table cannot produce this: its `count` is per-REQUEST while `hit_count` is per-sequence, so the two columns are different units.

panels.title: 5xx rate (24h)
panels.description: `or vector(0)` matters: with no 5xx at all the numerator has no series and the panel would read 'No data', which is ambiguous on an error-rate tile -- you cannot tell 0% from broken. clamp_min avoids divide-by-zero on a quiet day.

panels.title: OSDF verify in-flight
panels.description: Compare with verify_concurrency (4). Pinned at 4 with a flat fetch rate is the signature of a hung `pelican object get` -- the timeout covers only the queue wait, not the fetch.

panels.title: DB pool checked out
panels.description: Saturation is 60 (pool_size 20 + max_overflow 40).

panels.title: Token issue failures
panels.description: `pelican token create` has no timeout and no retry. If this climbs, no OSPool job can upload -- while /healthz stays green.

panels.title: Application errors by code
panels.description: AppError.code. 4xx codes (already_cached, upload_too_large) are client behaviour, not incidents; osdf_unavailable and token_issuance_failed are.

panels.title: Classifier outcomes
panels.description: 'unclassified' is a real no-hit. binary_missing / timeout / nonzero_exit mean diamond is broken -- previously invisible, since every failure path silently returns UNCLASSIFIED.

panels.title: Probe latency (/healthz 2m, /v1/stats 20m)
panels.description: /v1/stats is ~50x more expensive than /healthz (8 scalar subqueries over a 465k-row table), which is why it is probed at 20m. Its line is sparse by design.

panels.title: Reaper exposure - INFORMATIONAL ONLY (job is NOT scheduled)
panels.description: Entries past their source's idle_ttl_days that the reaper WOULD delete if enabled. It is deliberately NOT scheduled: on this instance reap() issues real `pelican object rm`. Read-only count.

panels.title: Host memory available
panels.description: Zero swap on this host, so this is the OOM precursor.
